1.bug_scenario: The bug concerns accessibility of the Toggle component in the Carbon Design System. Although the `aria-label` prop is required and provided, screen readers do not pick up or read the label as expected, making it inaccessible to vision-impaired users. Users often fall back on other label props ('labelA', 'labelB', or 'labelText'), but they do not solve the problem as those are either not available to screen readers or are not set as required. The screenshot demonstrates usage where the toggle is not announced properly to assistive technologies, violating WCAG 2.1 (SC 3.3.2).

2.explanation: The main logic for the Toggle component resides in packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js. A fix must occur here to ensure the aria-label is passed to the control and read by screen readers. The story file (Toggle-story.js) and test file (Toggle-test.js) are also relevant, as any change to prop handling or accessibility requires update or addition of usage examples and test coverage to ensure the accessibility fix works and does not break existing behavior.
2.bug_scenario: The bug concerns the Carbon Design System's Toggle component not properly applying the aria-label property for screen readers. According to the bug report and the demo GIF, even when aria-label is provided to the Toggle, it is not being read by VoiceOver, making the toggle inaccessible for users relying on assistive technology. Instead, the component only uses the visible label text or labelA/labelB props, which are either not required or bypassed by screen readers.
